en: The Zen Master Sōtai received this oral transmission from the Tang National Teacher:
Regarding the Fundamental Seal of Mahāpratisarā (First): Interlace the fingers of both hands with the palms facing inward.
Join and extend the two middle fingers. Position the two index fingers behind the middle fingers.
Slightly bent like a hook.
Joining the two little fingers and the two thumbs together and holding them upright, slightly bent, it is formed.

In Sanskrit, this is called *vajra*; in the language of Tang, it means "five-pronged vajra scepter. Second, the Heart Mantra of All Tathāgatas: With both hands, the left is inverted and the right is palm-up, with the backs touching.
The middle fingers are hooked back-to-back and held upright like an axe;

this constitutes the *balaśu* (Sanskrit), which in Chinese is called "battle-axe" (*yuefu*), and in Tibetan is called "the two hands standing back-to-back with the middle fingers hooked together. Third, the Heart-Seal Mantra of All Tathāgatas: Interlace the two hands internally and touch the tips of the two middle fingers together; bend them into a circle, and it is accomplished.
In Sanskrit: *vara-prasāda*; in Chinese (Táng): "Suo" (索). The Mantra and Seal of the Vajra Armor of All Tathāgatas, Number Four: Join the two hands in *añjali* (palms together).
Bend the middle joints of both index fingers so they are flat and level;
when the tips touch one another, it is formed.
In Sanskrit this is called *khaḍga*; in Chinese (Táng) it means "sword. This is the fifth seal for the Consecration Mantra of all Tathāgatas. Interlace the two hands with the backs facing outward.
Join the two ring fingers together and extend them upward;
cross the two little fingers upright, and it is thus formed.

In Sanskrit, this is called *cakraka* (pronounced *cakra*), and in Chinese, it is called "wheel. This is the sixth mudrā for the mantra of the boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*) of all Tathāgatas. For the second [mudrā], pinch the tips of the nails of the two little fingers with the two thumbs.
The remaining fingers are extended and joined together in the shape of a trident; this constitutes the seal.

In Sanskrit it is called *triśūla*, and in Chinese (Tang) it is called "three-pronged fork. This is the seventh seal for the Heart-to-Heart Mantra of all Tathāgatas: with both hands, cross them outwardly.
The two index fingers touch and press against each other like the shape of a jewel;
the two thumbs are held upright side by side, and it is thus formed.

In Sanskrit it is called *cintāmaṇi*; in the Tang language it is "Jewel. This is the eighth seal of the *Sarvatathāgata-cittamantra* (the Heart Mantra of All Tathāgatas). With the left hand facing upward at the heart, extend the five fingers.
Place the right hand over the left, joining them so that they are level; this constitutes it.

In Sanskrit, it is called *Mahā-vijayā-dhāraṇī* (in some traditions, *Mahā-vijaya-dhāraṇī*). In Chinese, it is translated as "Great Brightness Dhāraṇī. This is the Great Peacock Seal of Master Cijue, the Great Amoghapāśa Seal. It is the same as the five-pronged seal formed by the inner-binding (*antarbaddha*) gesture.
The Seal of Uṣṇīṣavijayā Buddha: Join the palms with hollowed centers.

Bend the two middle phalanges (anāmikās) so that they touch at their tips, and press the sides of the two index fingers (tarjanīs) against them in the manner of snapping the fingers. This is according to the text of the original ritual manual.
The Mañjuśrī Root Mudrā: Join the palms with the hollows facing each other.
Cover the two *tejas* (fire) fingers.

Bring the tips of the two *āpa* (water) fingers together and bend them. Cross the two *vāyu* (wind) fingers and place the two *ākāśa* (space) fingers on top. Furthermore, it is said that one forms the inner *bandha* (inner bind), joins the two *pṛthivī* (earth) fingers, extends them upward, and bends the two *vāyu* fingers across the two *ākāśa* fingers on top.
The mudrā of the phrase of fulfillment: join the two earth fingers like a needle;
the two water fingers hook inward;
the two fire fingers are like jewels.
The two winds are bent and pinched above the two *uṣṇīṣas*.
The mantra is: *avira hūṃ khaṃ*.
Transmitted on the twenty-second day of the third month in the nineteenth year of the Zhenguan era.
